title: Tiller rollout lifecycle brief and observation log (Mar 2028) - draft
content:
Purpose:
This doc is the operational brief for the 'Tiller' micro-release (service routing and model-variant selector tweaks). It combines the rollout calendar, hour-by-hour shift plan, preflight checklist, telemetry gates, and a living observation log for the 72-hour launch window. Goal: ship without user-visible regressions, stay within latency SLOs, and validate new fallback policy.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted API, dedicated pools, and edge-proxy routing changes.
- Includes model-routing config change v2028-03-tiller (feature flagged).
- Excludes on-prem install procedures (separate private deployment runbook).

TL;DR:
- Canary start: 2028-03-12 09:00 PDT
- Canary traffic: initial 1% -> ramp to 10% over 3 hours -> 50% over next 6 hours if gates pass
- Full ramp to 100% target on 2028-03-14 03:00 UTC contingent on automated quality checks and manual sign-off
- Rollback window: immediate 0. Backout plan available to revert routing within 5 minutes.

Preflight checklist (to be completed 48–2 hours before start):
[ ] Release artifact built: tiller-service:2028-03-05-rc1 (sha: a1b2c3d)
[ ] Integration tests green (stability, routing unit tests)
[ ] Load sim run (10% of expected canary traffic) - baseline verified
[ ] Telemetry dashboards deployed and quiet-window sampling configured
[ ] Canary host allocations reserved in Dedicated pool (ids: ded-east-23, ded-west-19)
[ ] Communication: Slack #release-tiller pinned, incident channel ready, escalation contacts confirmed
[ ] Pager duty rota: Lea (primary), Miguel (secondary), Aisha (on-call support)

Canary sizing and schedule (local times shown):
- 2028-03-12 09:00 PDT: Start 1% traffic (10 agents)
- 09:30 PDT: health check and model output regression job (50k prompts sample)
- 10:00 PDT: conditional ramp to 5% (if error rate < 0.5% and P50 latency delta < 20ms)
- 11:30 PDT: conditional ramp to 10% (pass same gates)
- 13:00 PDT: catch-up validation and manual review snapshot (release engineers & ML QA)
- 16:00 PDT: slow ramp to 25% if all gates pass; otherwise hold and investigate for up to 2 hours
- 2028-03-13 01:00 PDT: decision to continue to 50% or roll back
- 2028-03-14 03:00 UTC: target full roll if no regressions

Telemetry gates (automated):
- Error rate (5xx + service-level failures): must not exceed baseline + 0.3% over 15m window
- Latency: P50 delta <= +20ms, P95 delta <= +80ms vs baseline (15m rolling)
- Quality: sampling run (50k prompts) content drift measured; semantic-similarity A/B test p-value > 0.05 in the first two samples
- Resource: GPU utilization per node < 85% sustained; queue length < 20 requests
If any gate fails, automatically throttle to previous traffic percentage and open incident.

Manual decision points:
- 3-hour checkpoint after initial ramp (Lea + Miguel): review sampling artifacts and logs, decide to continue to 50%
- 24-hour review: product + ML leads confirm user visible metrics (CTR, latency, failure rates)

Rollback matrix (fast paths):
- Hot rollback to previous routing config: runtime flag flip (approx 2–5 minutes to validate)
- Full service revert: redeploy tiller-service:2028-02-28-stable (expected 8–12 minutes)
- If rollback initiated, notify #release-tiller and start postmortem template (link in linked_artifacts)

Communication & escalation plan:
- Slack: #release-tiller (ops chatter), #release-tiller-incident (incident comms)
- PagerDuty: primary escalation to on-call SRE -> release engineer -> product owner
- Customer notifications (only if user-visible regression detected): draft email + status page update template stored in confluence:Status-Templates

Smoke tests (automated run order, pass/fail criteria):
1) Route sanity: sample 1k requests across regions -> all responses within 2x baseline latency -> pass
2) Model variant selection: for seeded prompts, ensure expected variant chosen 98% of time
3) KV cache correctness check: compare cache hit rates against baseline +/- 10%
4) Fallback integrity: deliberately induce a single-host failure in canary group -> traffic should fall back to next compatible variant within 3s

Release notes (draft for public and internal):
- Public short blurb (user-facing):
  "We deployed Tiller v2028-03 to improve routing resilience and lower tail latency on multi-variant model queries. No changes to API surface; improvements are behind the same API and start rolling globally under a gradual canary."

- Internal release notes (for support/ops):
  - What changed: routing policy now prefers warm-xquant variants for short-context queries and applies a new heuristics-based fallback when memory pressure > 70%
  - Risk areas: fallback logic complexity may surface rare variant selection mismatches; watch 'fallback-rate' and 'variant-selection-entropy' metrics
  - Rollback steps: (1) flip runtime flag 'tiller-routing-enabled' to false; (2) redeploy tiller-service:2028-02-28-stable if flag flip does not clear errors

Post-release observation log (live during rollout):
- 2028-03-12 09:05 PDT — Initial canary: API 200s OK, small increase in P95 noted (+12ms). Action: monitor, no throttles
- 2028-03-12 09:45 PDT — Sampling run complete: semantic drift within expected bounds; 2% of prompts flagged for manual review (prompts with hallucination-like artifact). Action: ML QA to triage set A for deeper eval
- 2028-03-12 10:12 PDT — One canary node OOM (ded-east-23-host-4). Automatic restart succeeded. Short spike in errors for 90s. Action: mark host, increase eviction buffer on similar hosts
- 2028-03-12 12:50 PDT — Telemetry gate borderline: P95 = +78ms (threshold 80ms). Held ramp; manual review started. Action: reduced batch window on canary nodes; continued monitoring

Initial findings summary (so far):
- Tiller's fallback reduces error amplification during upstream model throttling; good sign for multi-variant stability
- Memory footprint variability across quantized variants needs attention (follow-up engineering ticket created)

Open action items (owners and ETA):
- AV-1294: Investigate OOM pattern on ded-east-23 hosts (Ravi Patel) — ETA 2028-03-15
- ML-351: Review flagged example set A for hallucination patterns and produce a follow-up eval set (Aisha Gupta) — ETA 2028-03-14
- INF-880: Add fallback-rate and variant-selection-entropy to daily alerting (Miguel Torres) — ETA 2028-03-18

Postmortem trigger criteria (if any are hit during rollout):
- Sustained user-visible error rate increase > 0.5% for > 30 minutes
- Repeated rollback within 24 hours
- Degradation in quality metrics with p-value < 0.01 on two successive sampling runs

Appendix: quick commands & helpers
- Flip routing flag (fast rollback): kubectl -n prod exec config-applier -- toggle-flag tiller-routing-enabled=false
- Examine canary logs: ./bin/logtail --service tiller --filter canary --since 2h
- Run sampling job manually: ./scripts/run_sampling.sh --suite tiller-canary --samples 50000

Notes to self:
- Keep the canary small overnight if telemetry becomes noisy; prefer slower ramps with manual review rather than aggressive automation when quality signals are weak.
- Keep a short internal retrospective within 48 hours of full rollover to annotate checklist gaps.

Document history:
- Drafted 2028-03-05 by Lea Chen
- Updated 2028-03-10 with early canary observations and initial action items

(End of doc)
